chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'The wergild of the erroneous (killing) is to be paid off within three years, and the wergild of the deliberate (killing) is to be paid off within one year.'

key_terms.تُسْتَأْدَى: To be paid off in installments

ai.seo_question: What is the time limit for paying blood money for accidental versus deliberate killing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the statutory periods for fulfilling the financial liability of blood money (diyah), distinguishing between the three-year grace period for accidental homicide and the one-year period for deliberate killing. It reflects the jurisprudential principle that the severity of the intent influences the urgency of the compensation, a ruling derived from the practices of Imam Ali (AS) and codified in Shia fiqh. This distinction underscores the balance between justice for the victim's family and the practical capacity of the liable party to pay.
